episode.title: Register a model generation's token capabilities in authoritative and browser-safe catalogs
episode.before: At parent 3a014e2afe2bc996ac4d61ca7aef660d26226f29, the core input catalog had only the broad /^kimi-/ 262,144-token rule and no output rule for kimi-k3, so tokenLimit('kimi-k3') resolved to 262,144 and tokenLimit('kimi-k3', 'output') fell back to 32,000. The browser-safe companion contained the same omissions.
episode.after: At 945cf3c8296f895871b6c087ac2a89d339cb9727, a /^kimi-k3/ rule precedes the broad family input fallback and maps the generation to 1,000,000 tokens; a corresponding output rule maps it to 131,072 tokens. Both rules are duplicated in the browser-safe companion catalog, preserving its documented synchronization contract with core.
episode.diff: The implementation adds four ordered metadata entries and changes no executable lookup algorithm: two entries in the authoritative core catalog and matching input/output entries in the browser-safe companion. No test file was changed, and the existing token-limit tests at the pinned ref do not contain kimi-k3 assertions.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 945cf3c8296f895871b6c087ac2a89d339cb9727 has parent 3a014e2afe2bc996ac4d61ca7aef660d26226f29 and describes correcting a 1M context window and 128K default maximum output that previously fell through to generic limits.
In the parent core catalog, the first matching input rule for kimi-k3 was the broad /^kimi-/ rule mapped to LIMITS['256k'], while OUTPUT_PATTERNS had no kimi-k3 entry.
The core catalog adds /^kimi-k3/ before the broad family input fallback with LIMITS['1m'] and adds an output rule with LIMITS['128k'].
evidence_units.source: git diff 3a014e2afe2bc996ac4d61ca7aef660d26226f29 945cf3c8296f895871b6c087ac2a89d339cb9727 -- packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts; pinned file lines 221-225 and 271-273

evidence_units.claim: The ordered lookup normalizes a model identifier, scans the selected pattern array from first to last, and returns the first match; otherwise tokenLimit uses the generic input or output default.
evidence_units.source: git show 945cf3c8296f895871b6c087ac2a89d339cb9727:packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts, findTokenLimit and tokenLimit definitions following lines 276 and 319

evidence_units.claim: The core tokenLimit API documents that it is used during configuration initialization to auto-detect input and output limits, after which configured contextWindowSize and maxOutputTokens are used.
evidence_units.source: git show 945cf3c8296f895871b6c087ac2a89d339cb9727:packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts, tokenLimit documentation immediately preceding its definition

evidence_units.claim: The companion module declares itself a browser-safe subset that replicates core constants and logic because the webview cannot require Node.js packages, and explicitly says it must be kept synchronized with the core catalog.
The companion catalog receives matching /^kimi-k3/ input and output entries mapped to 1,000,000 and 131,072 respectively.
evidence_units.source: git diff 3a014e2afe2bc996ac4d61ca7aef660d26226f29 945cf3c8296f895871b6c087ac2a89d339cb9727 -- packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/utils/tokenLimits.ts; pinned file lines 128-130 and 163-166

evidence_units.claim: The companion tokenLimit function is a webview fallback used when modelInfo._meta.contextLimit is unavailable; it selects input or output patterns and returns the first matching limit.
The existing core test suite exercises family input fallback and output-limit lookup for earlier Kimi models, but the pinned test file has no kimi-k3 regression assertion.
evidence_units.source: git show 945cf3c8296f895871b6c087ac2a89d339cb9727:packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.test.ts lines 251-256 and 368-370; git show --stat 945cf3c8296f895871b6c087ac2a89d339cb9727

evidence_units.claim: Direct evaluation of the ordered tables has a concrete oracle: both implementations should resolve kimi-k3 input to 1,000,000 and output to 131,072, while an older family member such as kimi-k2.5 retains its prior 262,144 input and 32,768 output behavior.
evidence_units.source: Pinned implementations at packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts lines 224-225 and 272-273 and packages/vscode-ide-companion/src/utils/tokenLimits.ts lines 129-130 and 165-166, combined with lookup semantics in E4 and E8 and existing expectations in packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.test.ts lines 251-256 and 368-370

evidence_units.claim: The evidence bundle identifies PR/issue 7144 as a verified implementation pull request changing only the two token-limit catalog files; PR discussion, reviews, and status checks are unavailable.

candidate_atomics.name: register-specific-model-capabilities
candidate_atomics.title: Register specific input and output capabilities before family fallbacks
candidate_atomics.description: Add generation-specific capability rules to the authoritative ordered catalog so lookup returns documented limits instead of broader family or global defaults.

semantic_action.intent: Make automatic token accounting use the model generation's documented context and output capacities.
semantic_action.pre_state: A model identifier matches a broad family input rule or the global output default because no generation-specific capability entries exist.
semantic_action.post_state: The specific model generation resolves to its documented input and output limits before any broader fallback, without changing sibling-family behavior.
semantic_action.validation: Query the public limit resolver for the target identifier in input and output modes and expect 1,000,000 and 131,072; also query an older family identifier and confirm its existing fallback results remain unchanged.

candidate_atomics.name: synchronize-isolated-capability-mirror
candidate_atomics.title: Synchronize the isolated consumer's capability mirror
candidate_atomics.description: Replicate the authoritative entries in a browser-safe catalog that cannot import the authoritative runtime module.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure an isolated client fallback reports the same model capacities as the authoritative runtime catalog.
semantic_action.pre_state: The isolated consumer duplicates the lookup logic but lacks the newly registered generation-specific input and output entries.
semantic_action.post_state: For the affected model identifier and both limit types, the isolated resolver and authoritative resolver return identical values while preserving existing fallbacks.
semantic_action.validation: Run equivalent input/output lookups through both resolvers and compare results for the new generation and an existing family member; the expected pairs are 1,000,000/131,072 for the new generation and unchanged legacy values for the existing member.

candidate_workflows.name: update-ordered-model-capability-catalogs
candidate_workflows.title: Update ordered model capabilities across authoritative and isolated catalogs
candidate_workflows.description: Correct stale model metadata by adding specific input/output rules ahead of broader fallbacks, synchronizing any required environment-specific mirror, and validating both the new mapping and fallback stability.

workflow_graph.goal: Make every in-scope token-limit resolver return the documented input and output capacities for a newly distinguished model generation without regressing older family mappings.
when_to_use: A recognized model generation is being classified by a broader family rule or a global default instead of its documented capabilities.
The repository has an ordered capability catalog and one or more isolated consumers that intentionally mirror it.
anti_goals: Do not change token-limit lookup, normalization, compaction, or request-clamping algorithms when correcting catalog metadata is sufficient.
Do not replace or widen the broad family fallback, because older or unknown family members must retain their established behavior.
Do not treat the provider's maximum configurable output as the default output value when the documented default is lower.
not_applicable_when: The model identifier is already supplied with authoritative runtime metadata that always bypasses the static fallback catalog.
The required capability values or identifier matching boundary cannot be established from authoritative documentation.
The secondary consumer can import and use the authoritative catalog directly and therefore has no independent mirror to reconcile.
inputs: A stable model identifier or identifier pattern
Existing family and global fallback expectations
workflow_graph.entry_state: The target generation falls through to less-specific metadata in at least one resolver, producing an incorrect input capacity, output capacity, or both.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Specific rules precede broader fallbacks in the authoritative catalog, every required isolated mirror agrees with it, and direct lookup checks prove both the new values and unchanged legacy fallback behavior.

steps.condition: Use when verified model capabilities differ from the currently matched family or global fallback.
steps.validation: The authoritative resolver returns 1,000,000 for input and 131,072 for output for the target generation, while existing family examples retain their previous limits.

steps.condition: Required because the webview cannot import the runtime package and explicitly maintains a synchronized browser-safe subset.
steps.validation: The isolated resolver returns the same input and output results as the authoritative resolver for both the target generation and an existing family member.

validation_ladder: Inspect rule ordering to confirm the specific identifier is tested before the broad family fallback in every input table.
Probe authoritative input and output lookup results for the target identifier.
Probe an existing family identifier to detect unintended fallback changes.
Run the same probes against each isolated mirror and compare results.
Add and run explicit regression tests for the new identifier in both modes; this final rung is deferred because commit 945cf3c8 added no such tests and the bundle contains no status-check evidence.
stop_conditions: Stop if the capability values are unverified or distinguish maximum configurable output from default output ambiguously.
Stop if normalization transforms the proposed identifier so the new rule cannot match as intended.
Stop if a required isolated consumer has different lookup semantics that cannot be reconciled by equivalent metadata entries.
Do not claim full automated validation until target-specific regression assertions or equivalent status-check evidence exist.
unresolved_or_deferred: No kimi-k3-specific automated test was added or present in the pinned core test file.
No companion-specific test file was identified for the mirrored entries.
PR reviews and status-check results are unavailable in the GitHub evidence bundle.

The commit message cites external provider documentation, but that external document was not included in the evidence bundle; the extracted numeric contract is therefore grounded in the implementation and commit record rather than an independently archived documentation snapshot.

unresolved_questions: Were target-specific tests executed outside the pinned commit? The evidence bundle has no status checks or review discussion.

Should the case-sensitive /^kimi-k3/ expressions use the case-insensitive convention used by some other catalog entries? Normalization lowercases input, so current lookup semantics support the implementation, but no target-specific normalization test was added.
Does every model name beginning with kimi-k3 share these capacities, or should the pattern be narrower? The inspected evidence supplies no variant-level discussion.
